recipes.name: Briam (Greek Mixed Vegetables in Tomato Sauce)
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place three of the tomatoes, the 1/2 cup olive oil, red wine vinegar, sugar, parsley, mint, basil, oregano, capers, and garlic in the bowl of a food processor and process to create a fresh tomato sauce. Season with salt and black pepper; set aside. Chop the remaining tomato; set aside.
Heat the 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet over medium heat, and cook and stir the onions until slightly golden, about 10 minutes.

Stir together the onions, potatoes, eggplant, zucchini, bell peppers, okra, the reserved chopped tomato, and the fresh tomato sauce, and place the mixture in a large baking pan. If needed, stir in a little water so that the vegetables are just covered with sauce.
Bake in the preheated oven until all vegetables are tender, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Briam (Greek Mixed Vegetables in Tomato Sauce)
raw_recipe.description: Mixed summer vegetables bake in a fresh tomato sauce, full of the aromas of fresh herbs, in this Greek summertime favorite.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! If you are using 1/2 cup olive oil, you don't need to add water, just cover the pan with aluminum foil. It should be done in about 1 hour or less at 400F. Serve with freshly baked bread! Thank you for the wonderful recipe!

Loved this! So amazed how much flavor it had. I switched the olive oil for broth and customized the veggies to our taste. After 3 tries we like it best baked uncovered for the last 15 mins to thicken the juices.
very yummy. Add-libbed with no zucchini, mint or capers. short on time, so microwaved till mostly done and finished in oven.

The fresh tomato sauce is delicious! I will 1/2 the recipe and NOT use water. I had to remove almost 1 1/2 cups of liquid. I will follow the suggestion in a previous review to cover with foil and not add water. This was a perfect side for grilled marinated lamb chops. Definitely will make again!

I was looking for a Greek sauce to go over baked meatballs that had feta and dill in them, so I adapted this and it was delicious! I only had fresh mint handy (snipped it off the new plant on my windowsill) so used a lesser amount of dried other herbs. Accidentally forgot the garlic and parsley, but dried parsley doesn't have a lot of flavor anyway. I only used 1 Tbsp capers, and used 2 cups of canned tomato sauce instead of the fresh tomatoes to make it quicker. Definitely a keeper!

Very pleased to see a recipe for Briam. This one is very good but a little too much oil for us (realize that you use a lot more Olive oil than we normally do). Anyway, cutting it back by a half worked just fine. Thanks for a good recipe.
Wonderful... and very flexible .. full of flavor very healthy too.. Thank you for this great recipe

This was simple to make and got rave reviews. I was a bit nervous about it because I have never made it before and I brought it to a party with my Greek friends. They loved it. It was all gone in 15 minutes. I will make it again.

Really great recipe. The subtle mint taste makes it different from other similar recipes. I didn't have okra and replace them with regular yellow beans. Perfect recipe to prepare when the veggies and the herbs are fresh. I froze a part of it to enjoy later in the winter.
I thought this was good but I prefer a regular Ratatouille over this recipe. a nice change and a good way to use up my garden veggies but not a favorite for me.
Delicious and healthy veggie dish! I didn't have most of the vegetables so I used broccoli, brussels and red pepper with the potatoes and onions.
This was the first time I have cooked using eggplant or okra and we all enjoyed this dish. Will make again
Loved this dish. Great flavor change and quick way to use up veggies. I added red potatoes.

I really liked this but bf didn't--not a surprise, since he doesn't really like tangy sauces. I also subbed a few different veggies in here but it didn't really change the overall flavor. Very easy, if a number of steps. If you like capers and vinegar you will really like this. thanks for the recipe!
